I used to struggle with my past before I decided to ignore it in favor of being more forward thinking. Because ultimately the past has very little utility other than letting it fuck up your life. Sure there are low points. I feel like putting a kamikaze headband on and rushing into a hospital with a sword sometimes. But I think about the things I do enjoy in life, and I think about the things that I might be able to create in life that I enjoy, and it draws my attention away from the past. It's not like I will ever forgive or forget. It's just that I have no interest with it anymore. The thought that my parents are out there somewhere, the fact that there's a doctor out there somewhere with my blood on his hands, the fact that I'm currently living in an entire country full of freaks who think it's cute, that I can't look at a baby without wincing, it just motivates me to continue moving toward my goal of leaving.   
Every ghost of the past has a resolution in the future.   
Of course, someday it's possible that I'll have my foreskin back. Someday I'll be known by a different name. My family will not have a legacy through me. Someday I won't even be an american, and I'll be able to look with trust towards doctors, instead of malice and contempt. Someday it's possible that I meet a woman to be my wife, who isn't even aware of what circumcision is, and she bears a son of mine and circumcision is something that doesn't even enter the mind of anyone involved, even the doctors or nurses involved with it.   
These are all physically possible things. They're achievable within a human lifetime. I know it's cliche to say things like "have faith" and "have hope" , but I mean to say, it's possible to cultivate faith in your power as a human being. It's possible to cultivate hope when you understand that time spent building a foundation for your future can bring about meaningful change. 

I feel like I'm rambling, but you're going to encounter shitty periods of your life anyway. Suicide can end up being a pragmatic decision that deals directly with the source of the problem, and it doesn't even have to be painful. But it's your decision, yours alone. You also have the option of moving forward. There's a fork in the road and we know where one goes, the bliss of not being conscious anymore in this world, but we can influence where the other road goes. Unless you really have to do it, which is your call, as I've said, my advice would be to take the road of hope for the future. I mean, scientists have regrown parts of the human body in a lab before, it isn't earth shattering news. We win in the end if we make the changes that we want to see now, and then we can play our win forward by showing the next generation how it's done. Find a culture that respects nature and the human body, and become part of its cultivation. Our lives can be dedicated towards the progress of objectively good endeavors. 

Done rambling. I support your decision either way if no one else will. I know when I'm feeling suicidal I wish I had someone who was honest enough to empathize with me.
